newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Lebanon expects three-year securities soon.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Lebanon expects three-year securities soon.

text.p: Lebanon is likely to start issuing three-year securities soon, but the final word on the timing of the new paper belongs to the finance ministry, central bank officials said.

Lebanon currently makes weekly auctions of T-bills ranging in maturity from three months to two years. They are denominated in Lebanese pounds and are the government's main source of public debt funding.

The Beirut daily ad-Diyar on Sunday quoted Ghaleb Abu Mosleh, head of the Bank of Lebanon's inspection department and a member of its open market committee, as saying three-year bills would be issued soon.

Interest rates would probably be a little above the rate for two-year bills which have recently fallen rapidly and now yield 16.14 percent per annum, the newspaper quoted Abu Mosleh as saying. The rate would depend on the time of issue, he added.
Asked to confirm the report, Bank of Lebanon interim governor Fahim Mo'dad told Reuters by telephone there was no official word yet on the new bills.
"We expect this issue but the matter is in the hands of the ministry of finance. We wait for their decision," Mo'dad said.
